title: AST diff tool
description:
## AST Edit Tool

### Background

Competitor analysis (`docs/COMPETITOR_IMPROVEMENTS.md`) shows that leading coding agents (OpenCode, Claude Code, Roo Code) avoid diff/patch hallucinations by using **AST-aware or exact-string-replacement edit tools** instead of line-number-based unified diffs.

- **OpenCode `edit` tool:** exact string replacement — `{ search, replace }` — line-number drift is architecturally impossible
- **Claude Code / Roo Code:** post-compaction tree-sitter folding re-injects fresh file structure so the model always edits from ground truth
- **Root problem with `writeDiffToFile`:** any context drift (compaction, summarisation) causes hunk headers to reference wrong line numbers → silent file corruption

This story implements an **AST-powered edit tool** that lives in `src/codeIntel/CodeIntelTools.ts`, alongside the existing catalogue/scan infrastructure, because it depends directly on Tree-sitter (already wired via `src/codeIntel/internal/treeSitter.ts`) and the `CodeIntelLanguageStrategy` abstraction.

---

### Scope

Three new callable tools are added to `CodeIntelTools` (interface in `src/codeIntel/codeIntelTypes.ts`, implementation in `src/codeIntel/CodeIntelTools.ts`):

#### 1. `getAstOutline(path)`
Returns the structural outline of a source file as a flat list of named AST nodes (type, name, start/end byte offsets, start/end line numbers). Gives the agent precise ground truth about the current file structure before making any edit — no stale context, no hallucinated positions.

#### 2. `astEditNode(path, search, replace)`
Finds the first occurrence of `search` (exact UTF-8 string) within the file, validates it maps to a meaningful AST node boundary, replaces it with `replace`, and writes the file atomically. Returns a unified diff of the change.
- **No line numbers required** — model provides the text to find, not a position
- **Unambiguous match validation** — rejects if `search` matches zero or more than one location (returns candidates so the model can narrow the search string)
- **AST-boundary check** — warns (but does not block) when the replacement would produce a parse error so the model is informed of syntactically broken results
- Mirrors OpenCode `edit` tool semantics exactly

#### 3. `astRenameSymbol(path, symbolName, newName)`
Uses the Tree-sitter AST to locate all identifier nodes named `symbolName` within the file, renames every reference in one atomic pass, and writes the result. Returns a unified diff. Scoped to a single file (cross-file rename is out of scope for this story).

---

### Implementation notes

- All three tools read files via `fsp.readFile` (UTF-8), mutate the string, and write atomically (temp-file + rename pattern already established in `saveCatalogue`)
- Tree-sitter initialisation reuses the existing `initParser()` from `src/codeIntel/internal/treeSitter.ts`
- Language pack loading reuses `languagePackLoader.ts` for grammar selection
- The `CodeIntelTools` interface in `codeIntelTypes.ts` must be extended with the three new method signatures and full JSDoc
- Type definitions for `AstOutlineNode` and `AstEditResult` are added to `codeIntelTypes.ts`

---

### Tests

All three tools must have tests in `src/codeIntel/CodeIntelTools.test.ts` (following the existing `describe.each(testModes)` pattern):

- `getAstOutline`: asserts node kinds, names, and line numbers for a known TypeScript fixture
- `astEditNode`: happy path replace, ambiguous-match rejection, zero-match rejection, AST-broken-result warning
- `astRenameSymbol`: renames all occurrences within a file, leaves non-matching identifiers untouched

features.title: getAstOutline — file structure outline via Tree-sitter
features.description:
Add `getAstOutline(path: string): Promise<AstOutlineNode[]>` to `CodeIntelTools`.

### What it does
Parses the given source file with Tree-sitter and returns a flat list of named/significant AST nodes — their kind, name, and exact byte/line positions. This gives the agent a fresh, ground-truth snapshot of the file's structure before it attempts any edit, eliminating reliance on stale summarised context.

### Return shape (`AstOutlineNode`)
Add to `codeIntelTypes.ts`:
```ts
export type AstOutlineNode = {
  kind: string        // tree-sitter node type, e.g. 'function_declaration', 'class_declaration'
  name: string        // identifier text extracted from the node
  startLine: number   // 1-based
  endLine: number     // 1-based
  startByte: number
  endByte: number
}
```

### Implementation notes
- Call `initParser()` from `src/codeIntel/internal/treeSitter.ts` before use
- Load the language grammar via the existing `languagePackLoader.ts`
- Walk the tree selecting node types that carry a meaningful name: `function_declaration`, `method_definition`, `class_declaration`, `interface_declaration`, `type_alias_declaration`, `variable_declarator`, `enum_declaration` (JS/TS node names)
- Extract the `name` child node text for each
- If the language pack / WASM is unavailable, fall back to a regex-based outline (best-effort) so the tool never hard-fails
- Path must be project-relative; resolve to absolute using the project root

### Tool description (for agent guidance)
> "Returns a structural outline of a source file as a flat list of AST nodes with kind, name, and line numbers. Always call this before `astEditNode` or `astRenameSymbol` to get accurate positions for the current file state — never rely on positions from summarised history."

features.title: astEditNode — exact-string AST-aware file edit (no line numbers)
features.description:
Add `astEditNode(path: string, search: string, replace: string): Promise<AstEditResult>` to `CodeIntelTools`.

This is the core tool of the story. It mirrors the **OpenCode `edit` tool** semantics exactly and makes line-number drift architecturally impossible — the model supplies the exact text to find, not a position.

### Return shape (`AstEditResult`)
Add to `codeIntelTypes.ts`:
```ts
export type AstEditResult = {
  /** Unified diff of the applied change, suitable for display. */
  diff: string
  /** True when the post-edit parse produced ERROR nodes — edit was still applied. */
  hasParseErrors: boolean
  /** Human-readable warning when hasParseErrors is true. */
  warning?: string
}
```

On failure (zero or multiple matches) the tool **throws a structured error** (do not return a result) with:
```ts
{
  code: 'NO_MATCH' | 'AMBIGUOUS_MATCH',
  message: string,
  /** For AMBIGUOUS_MATCH: up to 5 line numbers where the string was found. */
  matchLines?: number[],
}
```

### Behaviour contract
1. **Read** the file (UTF-8) from the project-relative `path`.
2. **Count occurrences** of the exact `search` string.
   - 0 occurrences → throw `{ code: 'NO_MATCH', message: '...' }`
   - ≥ 2 occurrences → throw `{ code: 'AMBIGUOUS_MATCH', matchLines: [...] }`
3. **Replace** the single occurrence with `replace`.
4. **Parse** the resulting content with Tree-sitter; set `hasParseErrors: true` if `ERROR` or `MISSING` nodes appear.
5. **Write atomically** using the temp-file+rename pattern from `saveCatalogue`.
6. **Return** `AstEditResult` with a unified diff (built with the `diff` npm package already used in `FileTools.ts`).

### Implementation notes
- Reuse `initParser()` and language pack loading already present in `CodeIntelTools.ts`
- Atomic write: same temp-file+rename pattern as `saveCatalogue` (already in `CodeIntelTools.ts`)
- Unified diff: use `createPatch` from the `diff` package (already imported in `FileTools.ts`)
- Path validation: must be within project root (reuse `isWithinRoot` from `fileHelpers.ts`)
- Do **not** block the write on parse errors — only warn. The agent may intentionally make intermediate broken states.

### Tool description (for agent guidance)
> "Replaces an exact string in a file with no line numbers required. Provide the literal text to find (`search`) and the replacement (`replace`). Fails with NO_MATCH if the string is not found, or AMBIGUOUS_MATCH if it appears more than once (narrow the search string to include more surrounding context). Always call `getAstOutline` first to confirm the current file structure."

features.title: astRenameSymbol — AST-driven single-file symbol rename
features.description:
Add `astRenameSymbol(path: string, symbolName: string, newName: string): Promise<AstEditResult>` to `CodeIntelTools`.

Walks the Tree-sitter AST for the given file, finds every `identifier` node whose text exactly equals `symbolName`, replaces them all in a single atomic pass, and writes the result back. Returns a unified diff.

### Behaviour contract
1. **Read** the file (UTF-8).
2. **Parse** with Tree-sitter via `initParser()` + language pack.
3. **Collect** all `identifier` nodes (and `type_identifier` for TS) whose text equals `symbolName`. Record their byte offsets.
4. If **zero** matches found → throw `{ code: 'NO_MATCH', message: '...' }`.
5. **Apply** replacements in **reverse byte order** (highest offset first) so earlier offsets remain valid as the string is mutated.
6. **Parse** the result; flag `hasParseErrors` if ERROR/MISSING nodes appear.
7. **Write atomically** (temp-file+rename).
8. **Return** `AstEditResult` with diff and `replacementCount` (how many identifiers were renamed).

### Scope constraint
- **Single-file only** — cross-file rename is out of scope for this story.
- Does not follow re-exports or type references in other files.
- String literals that happen to contain `symbolName` are **not** renamed (AST node type filter ensures only identifier nodes are matched).

### Implementation notes
- Byte-offset traversal: use `tree.walk()` or a recursive DFS over `node.children`
- Reverse-order replacement: collect all `[startByte, endByte]` spans, sort descending by `startByte`, apply slices
- The `AstEditResult` type (defined in the `astEditNode` feature) is reused; add an optional `replacementCount?: number` field to it
- Atomic write and diff generation: same patterns as `astEditNode`

### Tool description (for agent guidance)
> "Renames every occurrence of an identifier within a single file using the AST — string literals and comments are untouched. Returns a diff and the number of renamed references. For cross-file rename, call this tool once per file."

features.title: Tests for all three AST tools
features.description:
Add a comprehensive test suite for `getAstOutline`, `astEditNode`, and `astRenameSymbol` inside `src/codeIntel/CodeIntelTools.test.ts`, following the existing `describe.each(testModes)` pattern (WASM mode + Native Fallback mode).

---

### Test fixture
Define a shared TypeScript source string used across all suites:

```ts
const TS_FIXTURE = `
/** Person interface */
export interface Person { name: string }

export type ID = string | number

export class User implements Person {
  name: string
  constructor(name: string) { this.name = name }
  greet(): string { return 'Hello ' + this.name }
}

export function greet(p: Person): string { return 'Hello ' + p.name }

export const VERSION = '1.0.0'
`.trimStart()
```

Write this to a temp file (e.g. `fixture.ts`) under the tmp root before each test.

---

### `getAstOutline` suite
| Test | Assertion |
|------|-----------|
| Returns an array | `expect(nodes).toBeInstanceOf(Array)` |
| Contains `interface Person` | node with `kind` containing `interface` and `name === 'Person'` exists |
| Contains `class User` | node with `kind` containing `class` and `name === 'User'` exists |
| Contains `function greet` | node with `kind` containing `function` and `name === 'greet'` exists |
| Contains `const VERSION` | node with `name === 'VERSION'` exists |
| Line numbers are 1-based and in range | all `startLine >= 1`, `endLine >= startLine`, `endLine <= lineCount(fixture)` |
| `startByte < endByte` | byte range is valid for every node |

---

### `astEditNode` suite
| Test | Assertion |
|------|-----------|
| **Happy path** — replace `'1.0.0'` with `'2.0.0'` | returns `AstEditResult`; diff contains `-'1.0.0'` and `+'2.0.0'`; file on disk contains `'2.0.0'` |
| **`hasParseErrors: false`** on valid replacement | `result.hasParseErrors === false` |
| **`hasParseErrors: true`** on syntactically broken replacement (replace `{` with `BROKEN`) | `result.hasParseErrors === true` and `result.warning` is a non-empty string |
| **`NO_MATCH`** — search string not present | throws with `code === 'NO_MATCH'` |
| **`AMBIGUOUS_MATCH`** — search string appears twice (write fixture with two identical lines) | throws with `code === 'AMBIGUOUS_MATCH'` and `matchLines.length >= 2` |
| File is **not modified** on match failure | disk file unchanged after a NO_MATCH throw |
| Returned diff is a valid unified diff | diff string starts with `---` and contains `@@` |

---

### `astRenameSymbol` suite
| Test | Assertion |
|------|-----------|
| **Happy path** — rename `Person` → `Contact` | result diff contains `-Person` and `+Contact`; file on disk has no remaining `Person` identifiers (per AST re-parse) |
| **`replacementCount`** correct | `result.replacementCount >= 2` (interface declaration + `implements Person` + param types) |
| **Non-identifier strings untouched** — a comment `// Person` or string `'Person'` is not renamed | file content retains the literal string/comment unchanged |
| **`NO_MATCH`** — symbol not in file | throws with `code === 'NO_MATCH'` |
| **Unrelated identifiers untouched** — `User`, `greet`, `VERSION` unchanged after renaming `Person` | file content still contains `User`, `greet`, `VERSION` |

---

### Structural requirements
- All tests live inside `describe.each(testModes)('CodeIntelTools ($mode mode)', ...)` so both WASM and Native Fallback paths are exercised
- Each test that writes to disk uses a fresh temp directory (via `beforeEach` / `mkTmpDir`)
- `createCodeIntelTools` is constructed with `{ root: ROOT }` — same pattern as existing tests
- Tests do not import Tree-sitter directly; they test only the public tool interface
